title: Trump Wraps Up Midterm Campaign at Troubled D.C. Reflecting Pool Site
snippet: Swapping traditional battleground rallies for a controversial D.C. renovation project, President Trump is making his final midterm pitch at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool—a site plagued by severe budget overruns and delays.
content:
WASHINGTON — In an unusual departure from traditional campaign strategy, President Donald Trump is set to deliver his final pitch of the midterm election season from the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday afternoon, shining a fresh spotlight on a D.C. renovation project that has been marred by cost overruns, delays, and political infighting.

Rather than barnstorming competitive battleground states to shore up support for vulnerable Republicans on the eve of Election Day, Trump opted to anchor his closing message at the iconic capital site. The decision follows a intense month-long sprint where the president held over 25 rallies across conservative strongholds, attempting to counter low approval ratings and headwinds driven by voter anxieties over rising living costs, high energy prices, and foreign conflict.

A Costly and Delayed Renovation Saga

The Reflecting Pool project has been a lightning rod for criticism since April, when Trump pledged to overhaul the monument in mere days using private contractors for roughly $1.5 million. However, the effort quickly spun out of control. The project wrapped up nearly three months behind schedule, with expenses ballooning to more than ten times the initial estimate.

Even after Trump declared the site finished in June, the pool faced rapid deterioration. Severe algae blooms choked the water, and its new liner began peeling away, forcing officials to drain the pool completely in mid-July for emergency repairs. While Trump repeatedly blamed external bad actors for the damage, federal prosecutors attributed the issues to substandard construction work.

The ordeal also triggered high-profile fallout within the administration. The Justice Department initially charged former Olympian David Hearn with damaging the pool, only to abruptly drop all charges after determining he was not responsible. The dismissal drew public ire from Trump, who voiced sharp disappointment in U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro for dropping the case.

Reshaping the Capital

The troubled pool repair is emblematic of Trump’s broader ambition to reshape Washington’s architectural landscape. Throughout his second term, the president has directed significant energy toward remodeling capital landmarks—from adding gold accents to the Oval Office and replacing the Rose Garden with a patio to constructing a new East Wing ballroom and planning a towering triumphal arch outside the city.

Despite pushback from critics who argue his focus on construction distracts from pressing legislative priorities, Trump has defended his projects, maintaining that the upgrades are essential to restoring grandeur to the nation's capital.
